name: Echo CS-305 / CS-306
blurb: Oregon's selection guide prints four loops for the CS-305 and CS-306: 12 and 14 inch bars, each in .050 inch and .043 inch 3/8 inch low profile. The drive-link count matches across the two gauges. The gauge does not.
notice: Oregon prints a dagger after CS-305 and CS-306. The guide text does not define that mark. Both gauges below are what the guide prints. The bar stamp is the one that is on your saw.
intro: The CS-305 and CS-306 are a pair in Oregon's saw-chain selection guide, printed together with a dagger the extracted guide does not explain. They are not in Echo's January 2023 bars-and-chains chart, which is why this page is the Oregon line and not a row copied from the CS-310. Oregon gives the pair four chains, and the pattern is the point. At 12 inches the guide prints S45, 45 drive links, .050 inch, 3/8 inch low profile, and also R45, 45 drive links, .043 inch, the same pitch. At 14 inches it prints S52, 52 drive links, .050 inch, and R52, 52 drive links, .043 inch. The length and the drive-link count are the same on both gauges. A 12 inch loop with 45 drive links can be the wrong chain if the groove is the other thickness. Counting links, or buying "the 12 inch chain," does not finish the job. The .050 inch chain is the S code. The .043 inch chain is the R code. Oregon's guide uses that letter to carry the gauge, and the number to carry the drive links. It does not print a file size on the line, so the file cell is empty. It does not print a bar part number, a sprocket tooth count, or a displacement. Those figures are not invented here. The dagger matters because other Echo lines in the same guide use an asterisk or a dagger for a condition the legend, as text, does not spell out. This page reports the four loops Oregon printed and does not promote one of them to "the" factory chain. If the bar in your hands is stamped .050, the S loop at that length is the one the guide associates with the model line. If it is stamped .043, the R loop is. A .050 inch drive link does not enter a .043 inch groove. A .043 inch drive link in a .050 inch groove has side clearance and can climb out. The CS-310 page on this site is a different saw, built from Echo's own chart, and it is not a substitute for this pair. The CS-352 and CS-400 pages are low-profile .050 inch saws with their own link counts, including a 16 inch conflict on the CS-400 that this pair does not have, because Oregon does not print a 16 inch line for the CS-305 or CS-306. Two lengths, two gauges, one link count per length.

bars.note: Oregon prints S45 for the CS-305 / CS-306 line: 12 inch bar, 45 drive links, .050 inch, 3/8 inch low profile. No file size. A dagger is printed by the model numbers and is not defined in the guide text.
Oregon prints R45 on the same model line: 12 inch, 45 drive links, .043 inch, 3/8 inch low profile. Same link count as S45. Gauge is the difference.
Oregon prints S52: 14 inch, 52 drive links, .050 inch, 3/8 inch low profile.
Oregon prints R52: 14 inch, 52 drive links, .043 inch, 3/8 inch low profile. Same link count as S52.

sources.title: Oregon Saw Chain Selection Guide: CS-305 and CS-306 printed with S45, S52, R45 and R52

sources_note: Oregon Saw Chain Selection Guide, read 12 Nov 2026. The dagger next to the model numbers is not defined in the guide text, so neither gauge is dropped. Echo's 2023 bars-and-chains chart does not list the CS-305 or CS-306.
